label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. No fault was injected: an evaluation case, a false alarm (week 6). Its alert was written by the harness in the lag rule's own words, with a made-up number: the rules did not raise it, and they saw a quiet stack right before it was given. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 9 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the case's right answer by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Its diagnosis named no action, so nobody was asked to approve one.

alert.name: ConsumerLagHigh
alert.summary: The ledger consumer group is 250 messages behind on the topic provider-events, all partitions together; the threshold is 50.

diagnosis.hypothesis: The symptom is not confirmed; this looks like a false or transient alert. Every container was created at 11:07:21, about 5.5 minutes before the alert, so the stack had just come up. Lag data exists only from 11:07, and the ledger group's summed lag is 0 at every point, including 11:12:54. One possible source is a short startup backlog: the consumers joined after events were already on the topic and caught up between scrapes, so no nonzero sample was captured. The alert rule may also read a different series or labels. The ledger consumer is healthy and posting at a rising rate. The money check passes all five invariants and settled in 0.24s, so nothing is stuck or mis-booked. Still open: I could not see the sample the alert evaluated, so I cannot tell a missed transient from a misconfigured rule.

evidence.shows: Summed lag for consumer=ledger and for payment-confirmer is 0 at every point from 11:07:54 to 11:12:54. No data exists before 11:07.
The lag metric's labels are consumer, partition, service_instance_id and service_name. There is no 'group' label.
The ledger consumer posts events at a rate rising to about 3.3/s, with a few already_processed. It is consuming, not stalled.
All containers are running and healthy with 0 restarts. All started around 11:07:21-29.
All services were created at 11:07:21 with normal settings: idempotent ledger handler, dead_letter for bad events, cents, v1 secret.
The money check passes. All 1097 events were posted exactly once, the ledger is balanced, and the ledger and payments match the provider. It settled in 0.24s, so there is no backlog.

proposed_fix.summary: Take no action on the services. Review the alert rule: check its series and labels (the metric labels by 'consumer', not 'group') and its 'for' duration. Consider a startup grace period so a freshly started stack does not page on transient lag. If it fires again, query klaxon_kafka_consumer_lag per partition at the firing time.

diagnosis.blast_radius: None. The running system is not changed. Any edit to the alert rule only changes how sensitive alerting is.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: Nothing to undo. Any later alert-rule change can be reverted to the current rule definition.
